verdict: T-Mobile grew revenue 7% to $23.6B and profit 27% to $3.5B, as postpaid service revenue rose 9% and customers spent more per account.

kpis.label: Adjusted free cash flow
kpis.note: +5% YoY (non-GAAP: operating cash flow less capex)

segments.name: Postpaid service
segments.note: Monthly bills from postpaid accounts — phones, broadband and connected devices on pay-after-use plans. Up 9% as accounts grew and revenue per account rose.

segments.name: Prepaid service
segments.note: Pay-in-advance plans (Metro by T-Mobile, Mint Mobile and similar). Down 8% from $2,625M a year ago.

segments.name: Wholesale & other service
segments.note: Selling network access to other carriers and resellers, plus other service income. Down 7% from $734M.

segments.name: Equipment
segments.note: Phones and devices sold to customers, often on installment plans. Up 13% — device sales are low-margin, which is why equipment costs exceed this revenue.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Everything else, including advertising and other smaller revenue lines.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative — stores, marketing, customer care and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The cost of the network, spectrum and equipment wearing out over time.

otherDetail: Other expense of $1,121M, net: $1,031M of interest expense, net, plus $90M of other expense, net.
oneTimers: UScellular merger-related costs were $129M before tax in the quarter ($98M after tax) — integration and restructuring from the August 2025 UScellular acquisition, excluded from Core Adjusted EBITDA.

Other special items excluded from Core Adjusted EBITDA were $38M of network restructuring costs, $14M of legal-related expenses and $131M of other net costs, including $50M for retail store closures in the quarter.
footerNote: T-Mobile reports a single Wireless segment, so the revenue split above uses the statement's revenue lines. Income-statement figures are from the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q; the earnings release (Ex-99.1) summarizes results and reconciles the non-GAAP measures.

takeaways.title: Postpaid is the engine
takeaways.text: Postpaid service revenue rose 9% to $16.3B. Postpaid accounts grew by 274 thousand to 35.0 million, and average revenue per account rose 4% to $155.73 a month.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped 27%
takeaways.text: Net income rose 27% to $3.5B and diluted EPS rose 34% to $3.22. Core Adjusted EBITDA — the company's preferred profit measure before network depreciation and interest — rose 11% to $9.6B.

takeaways.title: Cash flow stayed strong
takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow was $5.1B, up 5%, as cash capex fell 14% to $2.3B. T-Mobile returned $3.5B to shareholders in the quarter: $2.4B of buybacks and $1.1B of dividends.
